hacking.notes: RCE in a customer-deployed NextChat v2.16.1 instance on Zeabur's shared cluster (CVE-2026-7644, MCP authorization flaw); attacker pivoted over the shared-cluster internal network to a routing cache holding Legacy API keys, used a team admin key to read AWS keys (incl. a long-lived root key), granted cluster-admin to a service account and used an over-privileged maintenance DB credential to read the production database.

plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/24577
Scope: #24577 is about Zeabur's October 2026 breach but explicitly cites the prior August 2026 breach as a separate event; this record codes the August incident (distinct entry vector, date and credentials). The October incident is a separate record also closing #24577. Reviewer may drop this record if only the headline incident is wanted.
Template Hacking-ext-unknown, deviated because Zeabur's incident report (Sept 7, 2026) gives the method: hacking variety Exploit vuln (CVE-2026-7644, NextChat v2.16.1 MCP authorization flaw giving RCE) plus Use of stolen creds (Zeabur legacy API keys, AWS root key, over-privileged maintenance DB credential). Vector Web application (the exposed NextChat app) and Inter-tenant: the vulnerable app belonged to a customer tenant on Zeabur's shared cluster and the attacker pivoted from that tenant's container into platform internals; reviewer may reduce to Web application only. Integrity Modify privileges (attacker granted cluster-admin to a service account). Attacker also created AI Hub access keys (revoked, no use found) - not separately coded.
Assets: S - Web application (NextChat instance), S - Database (production DB), S - Other (routing cache, internal management service, Tokyo shared Kubernetes cluster). Hosted on AWS -> External Cloud Asset(s).
Data: account and AI Hub account information (Personal); project environment variable names/values incl. AI service API keys, cloud credentials, DB passwords, app signing keys (Credentials, API key). No counts published for August. data_victim Customer. State Stored (encryption not stated).
Discovery: Zeabur confirmed the incident only after an external report of abusive API key use (Aug 28 02:34 UTC, ~24h after first API requests Aug 27 02:34) -> external, reporter not identified -> Unknown. Abusive API key use -> data_abuse Yes and motive Financial (use of stolen API keys); reviewer may prefer Unknown motive. Actor unidentified, single origin.
Timeline: Aug 27, 2026 start; dbir_year 2027. Containment date not stated.
Victim: Zeabur (Taiwan), 7 employees per Cybernews -> 1 to 10. NAICS changed from 5112 to 518210 because Zeabur is a cloud hosting/deployment platform, not a software publisher.
Confidence High: victim's own detailed report plus BleepingComputer/Cybernews.

event_chain.summary: Exploit vuln in customer NextChat app (CVE-2026-7644)
Use of stolen creds; privilege escalation to cluster-admin
Production DB and env vars read

summary: On August 27, 2026 an unidentified attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-7644) in a customer-deployed NextChat instance on Zeabur's shared hosting cluster, moved over the poorly isolated internal network to a cache holding Zeabur legacy API keys, used a team administrator key to obtain AWS keys including a long-lived root key, granted itself cluster-admin, and read Zeabur's production database, exposing account information and customers' project environment variables (third-party API keys, cloud credentials, database passwords). Zeabur learned of it on August 28 from a report of abusive API key use. A second breach followed in October 2026 and Zeabur announced its shutdown.
